utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. I think it was a wise decision not to schedule any hearing for this morning. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber informs the parties that it has decided to grant the motion for protective measures for Witness 13; reasons to follow. We move into closed session, and that will be for a rather long period of time; this is to address the public gallery.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If I missed the -- I thought we're going address the Markac motion regarding Witness 82.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Far more matters on the agenda.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: There was an invitation yesterday by the Chamber to see whether the physician -- to be vague, whether there was an attachment to their filing about a doctor providing medical opinion, and whether that doctor was the treating physician of Went 82 or not, and it's very relevant obviously for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber would like to hear, of course. The Chamber is seeking further submissions on this matter. Now yesterday there was a suggestion that there might be a written response already. But it certainly was not promised. Mr. Hedaraly, is there or is there not?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: There can be one by tomorrow, given the problems this morning. The slight chances that we have could have had them done, evaporated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you think that the Prosecution could respond orally. If you're satisfied with that opportunity, the Chamber will be glad to hear your oral submissions on the matter. We will resume at 25 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One of the first things I'd like to do is to deal with the leftovers of the 65 -- of the MFI list. I do understand that a new list has been distributed, but I'm still working from my own -- my old list, so I hope that creates no problems. Although we ended up somewhere in the -- if I could say, in the Lausic area, there are a few matters which I'd like to re-visit. The first one is D1083, where we were wondering whether, meanwhile, Mr. Mikulicic, a translation had been received.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We are still waiting for the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it remains on the list. I then move to P482. That is, what pages, how many pages, are tendered into evidence? The Prosecution was seeking only ten pages, but then the parties would try to reach agreement on what portions would be tendered and what not. Has agreement been reached?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, in the last housekeeping session, and agreement was reached. All that was remaining was the technical aspect of uploading the right portions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has it been uploaded?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes, it is has. My case manager informs me that he has. So the introduction and the portions that the Prosecution wanted to introduce have been uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I don't know if anything has changed since the last time I looked at this, Your Honour, but there was a portion that we wanted to upload as well. And it was in there the last housekeeping session, so I assume it's still there. I have no objection. However I may come back and revisit the issue and ask for something else to be added, because in the meantime, a map has been added to the back from the book, which I was unaware of. I have no objection to the map coming in, but there may be other maps that I asked to be loaded in as well. But at this point -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... no objections to the portions uploaded, but you reserve your right it ask for additional portions to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Correct. Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you have you an opportunity until Thursday morning to verify whether everything is the same as it was before but on the basis of what you verified as being uploaded the last time. Mr. Registrar, I take it that nothing has changed since then. I see Mr. Registrar nodding no. Then P482 is admitted into evidence. I now move to the -- if I could call it the Lausic list of mainly bar-tabled documents, a list that starts at P2210. A general request -- or general question, Mr. Hedaraly. It was announced that the Prosecution would seek to have admitted to the 65 ter list many, many documents of this list. I -- it's -- I don't remember that I have seen such an application.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I believe that you haven't seen it, Your Honour, because it has not been filed yet. It should be filed shortly. Hopefully but Thursday of this week, or Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Shall we say not later than this week because otherwise --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Hopefully, and shortly, and to be filed still this week. Then, therefore, I will pay attention only at this moment to those bar table submissions where there appear to be no objections. I will go through them one by one. P2221. I'll always make a short pause, in order to give an opportunity to object. P2221 is admitted into evidence. P2222, is admitted into evidence. I'm closely watching you. P2225, is admitted into evidence. P2226, is admitted into evidence. P2234, is admitted into evidence. P2235, is admitted into evidence. P2236, is admitted into evidence. P2238, up to and including P2240, is admitted into evidence. I now come to P2241, where, during the last housekeeping session, it was announced that a shorter version, the earlier version being 518 pages, but a shorter version would be uploaded, and I was informed by Mr. Registrar that that was done by now. That's the ... Mr. Hedaraly, could you confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I believe that's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, you -- there was a shorter version uploaded, P2241?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The number of pages is down to 74, as I understand. Is there any objection against the now uploaded 74 pages of -- consisting of -- which compose P2241, which are documents received from the Republic of Croatia, in response to a request for assistance?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections by other Defence teams. Then P2241 is admitted into evidence. P2246 is admitted into evidence. P2248, up to and including P2253. No objections; therefore, is admitted into evidence. P2260, up to -- oh, no, and P2261, in the absence of any objections -- Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no objections; however, I do wish to note that we also have no objection to the daily reports, I believe we are in a range now of 2251 to 2259.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But let me just see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If they're not 65 ter exhibits, which I can't imagine that they are not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just check for a second. Earlier I mentioned 2248 up to and including 2253, that covers all the numbers in between. Then the ones that follow; that is, 2254, up to and including 2259, still have to be added to the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: On behalf the Gotovina Defence we have no objection to those being added to the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Even not knowing the reasons why they were added so late. Are the other parties also already in a position to express their views?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'd like to see what the Prosecution has to say about the reason for the late application to the 65 ter list, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So then it is on the record that are there are no objections against adding to the 65 ter list of these documents. I think I then dealt with 2260 and 2261. I said in the absence of any objections, and I intended to continue to say that they were admitted into evidence, and that's I have done now. P2263 and P2264. I hear of no objections; therefore, admitted into evidence. P2276, admitted into evidence. P2282 and P2283, are admitted into evidence. P2288. Again, no objections; therefore, admitted into evidence. P2301 and P2302, are admitted into evidence. P2311, is admitted into evidence. Then we have a few other issues. We have Cermak's fifth bar table submissions, numbers provisionally assigned range from D1332 to 1342, the latter number included. Any objections, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I misspoke, Mr. Hedaraly, because it ranges from D1332 to D1343, instead of 42. Would that change your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I will be frank. I was going fifth Cermak bar table motion. So there are no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then D1332 up to and including D1343 are admitted into evidence. Then I come to the Gotovina Defence bar table submissions, and I'll deal with them by witness to which they are related. The first being Alun Roberts. But before further considering this, we see document descriptions on the list, we see, however, and that's true for all three series of bar table submissions, no entry as to whether there are specific portions or specific elements in this documentary evidence which we should focus on or pay special attention to. That is because the Chamber invited always to point at certain portions or certain elements which would deserve our specific attention so that we could pay less attention to other matters. Mr. Misetic, is this because you consider everything relevant or everything equally relevant or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think, Mr. President, we obviously don't consider everything relevant but we try to title the documents according to what we think the relevance might be. However, we can review them again and try to focus it more if the chamber wishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you would --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: By topic, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... please Check that. For example, by topic, or if it is a long report, the Mazowiecki report, for example, whether we would have to go through the whole of the document, or whether you would, in relation to the testimony of this witness, would ask us to pay specific attention. It is a matter which takes you some effort.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And which will save the Chamber considerable time if we are fully informed. Therefore, I'd like to keep on the record that we verify at a later stage, could we say within a week that we hear from you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if there are any specific portions. And I have difficulties in -- in accepting that for all of the documents, of course, shorter documents may be perfectly clear, that for all of the documents, the description as such would give sufficient guidance for our focus on the subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine, Mr. President. If I may just ask one thing of the Registrar. We have noted that we made an error and D1355 [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because that is already P694, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I had that on my list as -- then we do understand that there are no objections from the Prosecution on this range which would be D1344 up till 1345; then number 1355 to be vacated being a duplicate of P694; and then the series continue from 1356 up to and including 1377. I'm exclusively dealing at this moment with the Roberts.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: We don't have objections to the underlying documents. There may be issues with the relevant descriptions, but that is something that we can talk to Counsel about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although, I think the instruction of the Chamber was that the description should be shown to the other party first so that they could comment on it, and that we did not have to -- when did you ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When did you receive the descriptions, Mr. Hedaraly?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I must say, Your Honour, I don't have the date from the top of my head. Maybe counsel can assist me. I think it was last week, early last week. But that is from memory. Could be longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Are we talking about the existing descriptions, or the ones I'm yet to do?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The ones as I find them now on bar table submissions of documents related to Alun Roberts. We received a --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The same day I sent to you, Mr. President, it was received by the Prosecution, and Mr. Waespi indicated they had no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because we also received the information there was no objection. But it is now ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if it -- I think it's my mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... no, no, it's clear. No objections against admission but possibly against description.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Exactly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I have understood you well. First of all, the -- the Chamber invited the parties to agree on the description in order to avoid unnecessary further debates but, of course, the descriptions as such are not in evidence. Therefore, D1344 up to and including 1354, and P -- D1356 up to and including 1377 are admitted into evidence. And, Mr. Hedaraly, the Chamber, where an opportunity was there to criticise the description which has not been used only in very urgent and important matters, the Chamber would allow you to come back to the description and then we'll see whether there's is any need to change them. Of course, if the parties agree on a change, then the Chamber will accept that as well. Next series, Mate Lausic, range from D1378 to D1391. We were informed that there were no objections against admission. Mr. Hedaraly, do I have to ask whether there are any possible objections against the description?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then D1378 up to and including D1391 are admitted into evidence. Then the Puhovski Gotovina bar table exhibits, ranging from D1392 to D1424. The Chamber was informed that there were would be no objections against those.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That's correct as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I'm -- we know that we still have to hear the Puhovski submissions by Ms. Higgins. Mr. Cayley, would that at this moment be a bar to deciding on these?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, I think it would, Your Honour. I think the Trial Chamber respectfully should hear from Ms. Higgins before you decide on an admission of these document, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then it's on the record that the Prosecution does not object to admission. Could I hear from Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The very same position, Your Honour. I'm not objecting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Misetic thinks that we're talking about the documents offered by the Gotovina Defence, but I'm assuming that we're talking about what you mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're talking about the documents -- I even read it, Puhovski Gotovina bar-tabled exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: No. We're not objecting to those documents, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ranging from D1392 to D1424 are admitted into evidence. Then I move to the maps. On the 7th of November last year, the parties have filed at joint submission on the division of Croatian municipalities, and the map attached to that was called Annex A and was admitted as Exhibit P1282. Now the Prosecution has asked that the map binder be admitted into evidence. And I think, Mr. Misetic, you wanted to check what maps were already admitted before you would respond. Could you give us your response now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In all honesty I cannot, Mr. President. I need a minute to research that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you get that minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I move on to the next item. On the 16th of January, in our decision on the admission of statements of two witnesses and associated documents pursuant to Rule 92 quater, the Chamber admitted, among other documents, UNCIVPOL incident reports. And I give the numbers: S2-95-484, which was 65 ter 4131; and S2-95-498, which was 65 ter 7029. These two documents, however, were already in evidence as P235 and P239, and they were admitted through Witness Elleby. I think we have not received a final list with numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: We are working with the Registrar to resolve all the small technical issues in 92 bis and quater statements and exhibits that are in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We put this on the record so as to make clear that there's no need to assign new numbers to the aforementioned two documents. Next issue is the expert report by Professor French. I think the parties agree that Mr. French qualifies as a witness under Rule 94 bis, and the Chamber understood that the Defence has indicated that it did not wish to cross-examined witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I think you said qualified as a witness; I think you meant as an expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As an expert, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, nothing as far as I can see at this moment further opposes admission into evidence. Mr. Registrar, the expert report of Professor French. Mr. Hedaraly, could you help us out as to how to find it? I take it that it has not been assigned -- it is not a 65 ter number because it is attached to a motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It's not, but I think that we have uploaded it. I will find the right reference. If not, we will do so shortly so it can be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The report of Professor French to which still an exhibit number should be assigned is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I do have a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would become number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will become Exhibit P2353.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P2353 is admitted into evidence. The Chamber invited the parties to agree on an explanation how to understand grid references and to report to the Chamber if no agreement would be reached. The Chamber would like to receive an update.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Yeah, we gave report. We have disagreement with the methodology employed by the Office of the Prosecutor. We will submit something in writing on the methodology that employed using X, Y, Z grid for the coordinates. The Prosecution has used a longitude/latitude, or longitude meridian method that doesn't translate exactly, so it accounts for some errors, but I do believe that we have been going back and forth, and Mr. Russo - and correct me if I'm wrong, Mr. Hedaraly - but I just think we parted company on the end result.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I think I can definitely confirm that the Prosecution and the Defence have parted ways. I think at this stage perhaps it is better to just have submissions on both sides, and the Chamber can decide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the Chamber would like to receive written submissions on the matter because it is not something to be easily taken from the transcript of a hearing. By the end of this week, since you have quarrelled about it quite a bit, you must certainly be able to formulate your position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could have just to the beginning of the week. I have some other matters I have take care of, if I could do that. It's a -- it may be, and it may be helpful for us to do a draft response and give it to Mr. Russo. Frankly, I think we're trying to get this right, and I don't think we're that too far apart. It does become more difficult when you move to other targets when you use different methodology. Be that as it may, I think it might be helpful if we present it in writing for what it is, give it to the Prosecution, and see --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: We would, of course, welcome that, and if that can resolve the matter, we are more than happy to cooperate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Even a joint submission on where you do agree and where you do not agree and what the position of one party is, and what the position of the other party is on one document, would certainly find no objections as far as the Chamber is concerned. At the same time, of course, parties are free to submit what they wish to submit. But it certainly will assist if you exchange already your views on the matter prior to final -- making final submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I will say, Mr. President, we have been trying to go back and forth, and this is not something we haven't been working on. I know that obviously with the witness we that we had this week, and both Mr. Russo and I were detailed off doing other things, but we have had information back and forth trying to resolve it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber expects submissions not later than by Tuesday next week. Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Would that be -- I mean my understanding now is that the Gotovina Defence wants to file a submission. They will first give us a draft. So if we disagree, should we also file the same day or wait for the filing and then respond? It's unclear me, just so I know what we have to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber encourages exchanges of view which would allow, if there's no way of finding a joint submission on the matter, even if there is some disagreement, that the parties would have filed their views on the matter not later than next Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I just -- can I ask, Mr. President, can I have till Tuesday to give my response to the Prosecution, and then Thursday if they disagree. I mean, just as a little bit of lead time for them just to analyse what we have in writing. I just have some other things going on unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it, as a matter of fact, that the chance that we would extensively deal with grid references with the next witnesses to come is --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It is unlikely, Your Honour. I mean, and frankly, the issue is we provided our methodology to the Defence. We have not got theirs yet, so that's why we can't file anything now even if we wanted. That's why, if we receive something from Mr. Kehoe as soon as possible, we will look at it and then we can see if we can meet somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We have explained to Mr. Russo exactly what methodology we're using, so [Overlapping speakers] ... [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers that all the microphones not being used are switched off in order to ensure an accurate record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We will endeavour to try to get it right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not a matter which if you would need one or two days more, and if our expectation that grid references are not core issues with the next witnesses to come, then most important is that the Chamber receives clear explanation of the positions of the parties. And if you would need until Thursday, Mr. Kehoe, that would not meet any great problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, we're having a hard time finding the discussion about the map binder issue. Is there any reference that we can have?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can see whether I can ... I have no date for you, but sometimes if you would seek for ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It's on the 22nd of January at one of the housekeeping sessions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: 14871, in that page essentially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that it was at a housekeeping session, and that was the 22nd of January. Then there was some unclarity about the lifting of the confidential character of the documents pertaining to Witnesses 8, 9, 19, 30, 32, 36, and 45. We received an indication that there was no -- there was no objection against lifting the -- that no protective measures are needed and, therefore, the under seal status of P631, up until and including P637 is hereby lifted. Still, an exhibit number has been assigned to Prosecution document 65 ter 2552. It's an interview with Mr. Cermak with the Globus, published in Politika, dated 30th of October, 1997. At the time, we were informed there would be no objections. Is that still the case, as far as all three Defence teams are concerned?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will become Exhibit P2354.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P2354 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: On that same score in that same bar table there was also 65 ter 3530. I'm aware that that was also tendered as an attachment to the Prosecution's motion to have the interviews, the suspect interviews of the accused Markac and Cermak to be admitted into evidence, but since it was part of the same bar table motion and there were no objections at the time if we can also have a number assigned to that one at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That makes mainly sense if we could take a decision on the matter. And the previous one, I looked at it again late this morning, so in order to have it fresh on my mind. I haven't done the same with the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Neither have I, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that we could ask Mr. Registrar to have it marked for identification, so at least we will not forget about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will become Exhibit P2355, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I think I dealt with MFIs and related subjects. Then I'd like to move on to the second item on the agenda; that is, a short statement which I'd like to read. The Chamber would like to make a short statement clarifying the procedure with regard to changing exhibits and translations in e-court. If a party would like to make a change to a document that has been marked for identification or is admitted into evidence, a request to this effect should be done on the record. The Chamber will then consider the request, and, if granted, instruct the Registry to make the requested change. In the case of replacing a draft translation by a final one and if none of the parties oppose the new version of the translation, the Chamber has authorised the Registry to make such changes. The Registry should inform the parties and the Chamber staff through e-mail of the change made. This concludes the Chamber's statement. Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just a few housekeeping matters while on the subject. One of them falls right within the guidance given with respect to P450. The wrong range of ERN was uploaded into e-court. The new one is ready. It's a matter of changing it. That was done in October of 2008. We got a response right away from the Cermak saying there were no objections. We haven't heard from the other parties. There were no objection to the exhibit. It was just the wrong pages, the wrong document that was attached to it. So if we could have that admitted on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No objections by the Cermak; no objections by any of the other Defence teams. Then the Chamber grants the request to upload the right ERN numbers. And invites the Registry to make the requested change.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: On this same issue --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just happened to be out of the courtroom just for a moment when the issue of the bar table submission came up regarding statements. As the court will recall there has been a reduction in the amount of pages that the Prosecution is referring to, and I have not had a chance to finish looking at what their reduction is, so that's why there hasn't been a response yet. That reduction or notification came on, I think, Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will come to that at a later stage. It's one of the items on the agenda which we still have to deal with.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can I -- one more housekeeping matter. There were two documents shown during the examination of Mr. -- I think it is a protected witness. I don't have the number, so I won't -- off the top of my head. But I have the transcript references. It was 65 ter 5284, which was addressed at transcript reference 9278, line 17 to 9279, line 18. And there was also 65 ter 5028 at transcript reference 8314, line 23 to transcript reference 89317, line 14. They were shown to the witness. I have this information from Mr. Margetts. For some reason they were not MFI, so if we can have them assign a number and, of course, we'll let Defence see if there is any objection, just so that we don't lose track of it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest that the only thing we do at this moment to assign exhibit numbers to these 65 ter numbers. We'll then hear from the Defence. The Chamber is unable to immediately check so many transcript pages. We can look at only one at a time. And I take it that the Defence would need time as well to consider whether there are any objections. Mr. Registrar, 65 ter 5284.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will become Exhibit P2356, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit P2357, also marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. These were the two only ones, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: There's one last housekeeping issue that I have. Is regarding P881 and P887. Apparently they are the same document. The reason they got assigned two different exhibit numbers was it was a 92 ter submission, then called up in e-court in court with another 65 ter number. So P881 should be the one that is kept, and we can vacate P887. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, you wanted to address this matter or another matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It is a matter that has already come up because we're working on the court map binders, and we missed that there is a problem with P450. So I will wait my turn until you have resolved this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, first, Mr. Registrar, P887 should be vacated after you have verified that it's the same document as P881. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We note that P450, the original is 9 pages, and the English translation is 124 pages. So there is something not accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that could not be explained by prolixity in the English language, would it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I would have to check, but that may be one of the issues why we had to upload the right ERN range which hadn't been done until -- it had to be confirmed by the Chamber on the record. But I have to confirm that that could very well be the exact problem that we had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we hear from you soon, and if you would give prior announcement as to what the suggested action would be, to be sent by e-mail to all Defence teams and the Chamber staff, that would certainly allow to us deal with it efficiently during the next ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, just while on that exhibit, we note that there may be some translation issues, so if we could just ask the Prosecution, and whatever final version is going to be that it be checked to make sure that the translation of the portion they wish to tender is accurate, obviously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But apparently have you some thoughts about translation which I take it you will share with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yesterday I had a document -- this in the spirit of getting rid of many MFIs as we can to short order. There was a document that I put on sanction that was given a MFI number. It has been now uploaded as 1D00-0812. It had been given an MFI number yesterday, D1429. Mr. Russo had no objection to the admission of the document, so I would just -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yesterday it was not uploaded yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, it is uploaded now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is up loaded now. D1429 in the absence of any --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Is that on the record? [Overlapping speakers] ... I'm just asking because I have checked with Mr. Russo, so if it's on the record, then I will take that it's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's see. Let's see. That is one of the advantages of good electronic systems, that we can check that immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar -- no, let's first deal with the matter at hand. One --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I have yesterday's transcript, the draft transcript in front of me at page 17, and Mr. Kehoe said at line -- page 17 line 13 if we could MFI it at this point, I will go get a doc ID number, we appreciate that, and offer it into evidence. It says objection, and it is very likely that Mr. Russo said no objection, so based on that, it's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You have a possibility to revisit the matter within 48 hours if it would turn out to be incorrect. D1429 is admitted into evidence. I further inform you, Mr. Hedaraly, that D88 -- P881 and P887 are not the same documents. There are handwritten additions to P881, which do not appear on P887. So, therefore, although the substance seems to the same, it's not the same document. Apart from that, there is apparently some stamp about the authenticity of the document or where it was taken from on P881 which does not appear on P887. So, therefore, the instruction to vacate P887 is not standing anymore. Nothing else on MFIs. I have another decision to read, but I would first like to give an opportunity to the parties to make submissions in private session. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Misetic although your name starts with M, just as the name of Mr. Margetts, I take it that the transcript will be corrected. The Chamber will now deliver its reasons for admission of Exhibit P231226 tendered through Witness Josip Turkalj. On the 15th of December, 2008, the Prosecution tendered from the bar table in relation to the testimony of witness Josip Turkalj, an Official Note, in relation to Slavko Turudic, which was subsequently marked for identification by the Chamber, after the Markac Defence objected to its admission, on the 18th of December 2008. During a housekeeping session on the 22nd of January, 2009, the Chamber admitted P1226 into evidence with reasons to follow. On the 30th of January, 2009, a decision on admission of a number of MUP Official Notes tendered through witness Zganjer was filed. The Markac Defence's objection to the admission of P1226 was based on the understanding that an Official Note is not a proper witness statement, as it is not signed by the witness, and the subject of the interview was never verified through the proper procedure, according to Rule 92 bis of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence. P1226 is the MUP Official Note in relation to Slavko Turudic, a member of the Lucko anti-terrorist unit in August 1995. The Official Note describes the impressions an observations of Turudic in Grubori on the 25th of August, 1995, and was, therefore, found by the Chamber to be relevant for Counts, 1, 6, and 7 of the indictment. The Markac Defence's concerns regarding the probative value of MUP Official Notes are addressed in a decision on admission of MUP Official Notes, filed on the 30th of January, 2009. No other argument challenging the probative value of P1226 has been advanced. Therefore, the Chamber found P1226 to have probative value, and for these reasons, the Chamber admitted P1226 into evidence. And this concludes the Chamber's reasons on the matter. I have one more issue on my list. The Prosecution has filed a motion for admission into evidence of statements of the accused Cermak and Markac and associated exhibits. The Chamber urged the Prosecution to reduce the size of the statements or at least to make a selection and to tender the most relevant portions. Meanwhile, the size has been reduced. The Defence asked for extra time. I think if we just look at the motion, then the time-limits would expire tomorrow or the day after tomorrow. Therefore, the Chamber has asked itself how much time should be granted to the Defence to respond. I think that the reduction in size may raise additional issues. At the same time, the fundamentals seem to be the same. Could I hear how much time would be needed to respond to this motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could have until Monday to file a response, I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the Chamber had Friday on its mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If it's Friday, then we'll work around it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I don't want to make it -- I mean if you say -- I mean we want to give a bit of extra time because the fundamentals remain the same and, of course, the reduced size of the statements may ask for some adaptation. Monday by noon. Would that be -- so that it would at least give you some additional time over the weekend.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that's what you're seeking, then, of course, if it would be filed on Friday, then mostly we would look at it during the weekend but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We will endeavour to get it filed by Friday; however, I would ask until Monday just because I have the witness upcoming, and I'm not sure in terms of my time how much time I have. But be we will endeavour to get it filed on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The endeavour is appreciated, and if it would be Monday by noon, then the Chamber would not for that reason alone, consider the response to be late. Any of the other Defence teams? Because I would ask Mr. Misetic, but I take it that the other Defence teams would --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We don't object to that amount of time being given, Your Honour. It is something that we could deal with fairly quickly. Have I been indisposed by illness for the last couple of days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can still hear in from your voice, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I won't say anymore then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: It's the same position, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So, therefore, the Chamber hopes to receive your submissions by Friday, and if not, to not receive it not any later than by Monday noon. Yes, I one additional matter. Is it true that we were informed that the OTP wanted to tender, or have we dealt with that already, 65 ter 0284 and 65 ter 5028, both?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can I just have some guidance on what those two are?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It should be an omission to tender documents which were used in relation with witness Kardum.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes, that was dealt with earlier, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... yes, I now remember numbers were assigned; it was MFIed, but the Chamber said that since it appears on a totally different part of my list, I made this mistake. Mr. Mikulicic, the 23rd of February report of Professor Folnegovic, I have that -- it has been officially filed with the annexes because I have a copy in my hands at this moment which seems to be a courtesy copy sent to the Chamber's legal staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It has not been officially filed. This is a -- only a response to your request from yesterday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have a cover letter which is rather brief and addressed by his first name to the leader of the Trial Chamber staff support which doesn't say any more than that you have appended the documents on which Professor Folnegovic Smalc has based her conclusions but attached to it is also a letter or a report dated the 23rd which is not mentioned in the letter. May I take it that you want to file the letter dated the 23rd of February, in which Professor Folnegovic Smalc addresses you and explains what of her documents were she had at the beginning, what six documents she further consulted when she -- what documents were used in preparing the second opinion, and added are two paragraphs in which you draw specific attention to certain aspects of it, and that's the letter where you said there were some incorrect translations. May I take it that it is this letter and the annexes that you want to bring to our attention. You're then invited to file them so that they are properly put on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: We will do so, Your Honour. But just -- just have in mind that there was an urgent matter because your ruling was only yesterday afternoon. In the meantime we have a huge problem in the morning with an electrical system and the computer system, so it was the easiest way to do it, but of course we will file it properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Mikulicic. This was not just comment just to try to get everything in such a way on the record, that those who might want to consult the record at a later stage are fully informed. Let me confer with my colleagues for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have two issues, just so you're aware of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have two issues. One is to respond to your inquiry earlier in the day about the maps, the binder. I have reviewed them. In principle I don't have an objection. However, some of the maps we think lack relevance. Others of them have errors in them, and I think if the Prosecution wants to admit them, we'll have to discuss with the Prosecution because there have been -- some of theme are created by the Prosecution, and I think, quite frankly, there are some mistakes in them that need to be corrected. The third issue is almost none of them are uploaded into e-court or have a 65 ter number, so they are as far as I know not on the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Which is why we had raised the issue in the last housekeeping session, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I looked at the transcript. I didn't see a motion to add them. But in any event I would be happy to talk to the Prosecution and see if there is agreement that can be reached on these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could reach agreement on this, of course, it may not be a secret that the Chamber looked at these maps quite often. Therefore, we would be assisted by any comments on inaccuracy of these maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And even they're not on the 65 ter list, I can imagine that the parties can agree that it is better for the Chamber rather than to draw and their own maps, to use maps that are not only in existence but also verified as to their accuracy, and to the extent needed, corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. President, the second issue is, I rise because of a filing by the Prosecution today. There is a motion to add two documents summarizing investigative steps taken by civilian authorities to the Prosecution exhibit list and to admit these documents into evidence. I don't know if the Chamber has had a chance to review it. It is 101 pages involving spreadsheets of what probably involve hundreds, if not more than a thousand, underlying supporting materials. We are probably about a week away from the close of the Prosecution's case. It is simply, in terms of our ability at this point to analyse or provide any review of the Prosecution's submission is for all intents and purposes at this point, impossible. So if the Prosecution has -- I'm sorry, if the Trial Chamber could give us some guidance the next time we meet on how you wish to deal with this. But this is not a simple exercise for us, and to do it now basically precludes us from reviewing. You know, in theory we would have 14 days to try to do something with this. Obviously that is not going to happen now, so any guidance from the Chamber on how to approach this, because I'm afraid that it may be the Chamber itself that is going to have to make -- make heads or tails of this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, any comments on --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Just very briefly. I'm not completely familiar with it; I know only a little bit. But I think the motion does describe what was done. Some of this was actually related to other issues about what we had about D511 and D568, if the Chamber remembers, on which a decision is it pending still. I would invite the Chamber to look at a carefully, and if the Chamber wants us to do anything in response, we will obviously -- obviously respond to that invitation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I can just add two things that I forgot to add. One is that the filed copy of the spreadsheets is virtually illegible at this point, so we would need a different disclosure from the Prosecution. The second is then there are -- there are exhibits attached which then try to tie the documents to some of the killing incidents. I haven't had a chance to now even look to see whether killing incidents that have been remanded back to the Trial Chamber by the Appeals Chamber are included or not. But in any event the whole issue of the prejudice to the Defence on the killing incidents in the first place would in addition now be compounded by the fact that we're now being given underlying documentation that's being tied to killing incidents less than a week or roughly a week before the close of the Prosecution case. So -- and I have already stated that I have enough trouble filing something by Friday. The chances of me being able to deal with this at any time before next week are nil. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I have just got some supplemental information int he meantime. And it says that the Defence had the bulk of this material since September when Witnesses Kardum testified.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think you gather from the reaction here that, you know, the fact that they disclosed 2.000 pages of paper to us certainly doesn't help us, nor -- the fundamental point is that they're not moving that paper into evidence; they've now created spreadsheets and are making claims on the basis of underlying paper, which of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Which the Defence has done as well from what I understand, and that's -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... and disclosed in the middle of the trail, giving the Prosecution plenty of time to review our spreadsheets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... we can easily establish two things before 7.00. Is that the first, that none of are doctors. And second that the Chamber will not -- not even having seen the submission, not even knowing whether Mr. Hedaraly referred to disclosed documents or documents already in evidence, the Chamber will certainly not decide the matter before 7.00. The Chamber will try to inform the parties as soon as possible, and we'll try to do it tomorrow morning, about how we proceed, and that's of course in relation to several motions, how we will proceed on Thursday. Whether we will hear the testimony of the witness scheduled for Thursday. If not, what our steps will be. We need some time to further consider the submissions that were made today on the matter. The Chamber will certainly not be able to issue written full reason decisions on the matter. The Chamber will decide the matter and will informally tell the parties what they can expect for Thursday. Is there any other matter at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As the Trial Chamber finds difficulty responding to as well to matters, I looked at the motion filed this afternoon with alarm and have set up a meeting tomorrow with my team and asked for ideas how on earth we deal with it. I think the Court will understand when they look at the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll have a look at it. Again, the only thing I know is now that it is apparently 100 pages or something like that, and there are spreadsheets in it, so we will have a lock at it. We adjourn, and we will resume, as matters stand now, resume on Thursday, the 26th of February, 9.00, in Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 26th day of February, 2009, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25
